findings.detail: RE-CHECK: the mismatch is confirmed, but the cause given in the first pass was wrong. The pipeline funnel's IN REVIEW column adds up to 75 (India 55, Sri Lanka 5, China 1, Nepal 5, Laos 1, Philippines 2, Thailand 6). The Review Queue and the nav badge show 73 (Sri Lanka 4, no China). Both numbers come from the same capture at 08:52, and overview._cached was false. The first pass blamed live_source_sql, but live_source_sql('rt') (shared/tour_liveness.py:30) is the same filter as the funnel's _ACTIVE_RAW ('source_status = active AND deleted_at IS NULL'), so that is not the cause. The real difference is the tenant: the queue filters rq.tenant_id = aa_internal (api/routers/admin_pipeline/review.py:141), while the funnel's rev_c (api/routers/admin_overview.py:72-78) has no tenant filter. The tenant pipeline (services/acp_produce/tenant_pipeline.py:628, services/jobs/t2_rewrite_job.py:358) writes pending review_queue rows under an agency's tenant_id. Those rows show up in the Master Content funnel but not in the AA queue. The 2 extra tours are therefore most likely tenant review rows. I could not confirm this row by row because the CIS session had expired (401) and the audit allows no DB access.

findings.proposal: Add `AND rq.tenant_id = $1::uuid` to rev_c in api/routers/admin_overview.py, the same aa_internal filter pub_c already uses, so the funnel and the Review Queue count the same pending set. Optionally also count rows rather than DISTINCT tour_id, to match the queue's COUNT(*). Add a unit test that compares the two SQL WHERE clauses.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED on re-check (not refuted). The page says 'Publish would be refused: The entity is inactive in Booking. Written for facts v1; Booking is at v2.', but the draft's main Publish button stays enabled (isDisabled=false, no aria-disabled, no title). A reviewer can open the confirm dialog and run into a refusal the page already knows about. Checked on a synthetic entity ('SYNTHETIC S280 guide 2 (not real)'); the page reads GET /api/admin/supply-content/{id} (200). Re-check, 17/11, with the saved CIS session still valid: the blockers box renders the same two reasons and Publish is still enabled. The write guard did not cause this: the button's state comes from the client render, and the only aborted requests were a Sentry envelope POST and POST /api/auth/refresh. Those two also explain the 3 'Failed to load resource' console lines, so the page has no real console errors. The text is current: the entity is inactive, it is on facts v2, and the draft was written for v1. The code confirms it: in apps/AA-CIS-App/frontend/app/admin/supply-content/SupplyContentDetail.tsx (around lines 194-207), <Blockers items={publishBlockers(...)}/> is rendered, but the <Button> inside data-testid='supply-publish' has no disabled prop. The backend refuses this publish: services/supply_content/review.py raises ReviewError(409,'inactive') and (409,'outdated'). The 'Publish again' path in the same file (lines 124-125, 169) already hides the button when republishBlockers is non-empty, so the draft path does not match it. No data is at risk because the server refuses, but the UI invites a doomed action.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED, narrowed. The same AWS account shows up under two names on one page. It never checks the connection registry. accounts.account_name() does check it (AA-1095 satellite_connections), and that is why the two labels differ. Cost Explorer only fetches acc2 and acc3 (FETCH_ACCOUNTS), and the stored rows for this account are pre-AA-998 history (window 18 Oct to 9 Nov, before S278). Its live Bedrock spend already appears in the forecast's Bedrock provider row from llm_call_log.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED, one sub-claim refuted. The stored per-account Cost Explorer snapshot is about 8 days stale. The AWS bill tab only covers 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-09 (fetched 11 Nov). findings.detail: CONFIRMED on re-check (not refuted). I reopened the live page on 17/11/2026 with the still-valid auth/booking.json and a guard that allowed only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. The page returned HTTP 200 and GET /api/booking/notifications?limit=20 returned 200. The audit guard blocked one request, a Sentry telemetry POST. Two GETs for /cases/TC-000034 and /cases/TC-000037 ended ERR_ABORTED. These look like cancelled Next.js link prefetches: the guard only aborts writes, and they do not affect the finding. The single console error is the Sentry POST that the guard blocked. The page still shows '74 unread', which matches unread_count 74. Of the latest 20 notifications, 16 are tour lifecycle events (tour.reinstated 11, tour.retired 5), and every one names the tour only by its raw CIS UUID, for example 'Tour 000e3340-d9f5-4b7b-8609-4cdaa9c272dc is served again; trip case TC-000028 can use it as before.' The one trip-plan entry is titled 'Tour back in the catalog: trip plan 000e3340', which is the first 8 characters of the UUID. Per-case titles use the case code (TC-0000xx), which is fine. Root cause is in the backend, not the frontend or the audit guard: apps/AA-Booking/backend/app/catalog/lifecycle.py `_notify` (lines ~189-235 on main 31b6122) builds every message from `source_id`, and the plan title from `source_id[:8]`. `data` holds only source_id/reason/outbox_id/code/status/via, and no tour title, so the frontend has no name it could show either. This is not stale text. The events are real (CIS outbox 78, 14-15/11), and the wording is what the code produces today. Staff cannot tell which tour moved without opening the case.

findings.proposal: When lifecycle.py builds tour.retired / tour.reinstated notifications, look up the tour title. catalog.v_tour has `title`, but a retired tour may no longer appear in v_tour, so use the title stored on the trip case leg or itinerary, or on the trip plan, as a fallback, and keep the UUID only as a last resort. Put the title in the message and in `data.tour_title`, and title the trip-plan notification with the plan's own name instead of source_id[:8]. Existing rows keep the UUID unless they are backfilled. The frontend could also render data.tour_title when it is present.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED on re-check, and the root cause is now found. The Seasons page shows 'Calendars 0', 'Tours with a calendar 0' and 'No calendar yet. The catalog sync makes an empty calendar for the destination of each tour's first day.' GET /api/booking/pricing/season-calendars returned 200 with no items. That endpoint has no tenant or role filter (seasons_admin.list_calendars only filters by an optional owner_kind), so the E2E session does not hide any rows. The live schema dump of 16/11 also shows booking.season_calendars at 32 kB, which is index pages only, so the table is empty. The cause is not missing day-1 destinations and not a step that never runs. The step runs and times out every time. Booking worker logs (/ecs/aa-booking-dev, last 5 days, read-only) hold 405 runs of bk_trip_plan_sync. All of them reported 'tours': 844 together with 'calendars': {'skipped': 'TimeoutError'}, and not one run assigned a calendar. Each run logs 'slow_query duration_ms=5000 budget_ms=1000 catalog=true error=TimeoutError' on seasons_admin.UNASSIGNED_SQL, then 'bk_trip_plan_sync calendars skipped: TimeoutError'. The latest such run was 2026-11-17 05:30 UTC on git sha abbf00e. UNASSIGNED_SQL does a JOIN LATERAL to catalog.v_tour for every trip plan without a calendar, then ORDER BY md5(id||salt) LIMIT 50. Postgres therefore resolves the catalog view for all 844 plans before the LIMIT, which goes past the pool's 5 s command_timeout (app/db.py). _calendars() in trip_plan_sync.py treats TimeoutError as a catalog error (CATALOG_ERRORS), so it fails soft and the job still reports 'succeeded'. The failure shows nowhere except a warning log line. Result: every tour stays on the default low season, with no peak uplift, festive validity or stop-sale. The empty-state hint describes the intended design correctly; the data is what is wrong. The 4 blocked writes on this page are Sentry envelope POSTs stopped by the audit's own guard, so they are not part of this finding.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED (re-check, not refuted). The tariff currency select offers USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, SGD and VND, but only USD, EUR and VND can price today. Picking GBP (likewise AUD or SGD) returns 422 invalid_currency ('no approved FX rate for GBP today; AA prices this tariff in USD, EUR, VND'), and the table shows the error state 'Could not load' with a Retry button that can never succeed. Live re-run was not possible: the saved booking storageState has expired (every URL redirected to /login?reason=expired), and a second sign-in was not attempted because sign-in codes share one mailbox. The finding is confirmed from the audit screenshot plus the current code on Booking main 31b6122 (17/11). (1) The screenshot shows the GBP select, the 'Could not load' state and the exact backend message under a valid e2e-booking session, so the failure is not a login or guard artefact. (2) The write guard cannot cause it: the tariff call is a GET, and the 4 blocked writes are Sentry envelope POSTs (the re-run blocked the same Sentry ingest POSTs and nothing else). (3) The code makes it certain: frontend/lib/api/agencyPricing.ts hard-codes TARIFF_CURRENCIES = [USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, SGD, VND] (= backend QUOTE_CURRENCIES), and TariffView.tsx renders all six, while backend app/b2b/tariff.py check_currency() refuses with 422 any non-USD currency without an approved FX rate in force (fx_rates_in_force). findings.detail: CONFIRMED, root cause found. At 390 px the document scrolls (scrollHeight 1351, viewport 844) as well as main.aa-admin-main (scrollHeight 1839, clientHeight 784), so the page has two scroll containers. Of the 390 px Booking detail pages in the same run (invoice, manifest, supplier edit, supplier contracts), only this one has a document height above 844. Cause: SupplierPhotos (app/(staff)/_parts/SupplyContent.tsx, around line 216) renders a hidden <input type=file className="sr-only">. sr-only makes it position:absolute, and none of its ancestors is positioned. The kit PageFrame <main> sets overflowY:auto but no position, so main does not clip the input. The input keeps its static position deep inside main's scrolled content and makes the document taller. The input renders only when canWrite && recordActive, which is why it shows on this page. At 1440 px the photo header sits inside the 900 px viewport, so desktop is not affected. Live re-open on 17/11 was not possible because the stored Booking session had expired (redirect to /login?reason=expired), so this is judged from results-extra.json and the code. findings.detail: CONFIRMED on re-check (live, 17 Nov 2026, saved crm.json session still valid, read-only guard on). A booked trip that departs 20 Nov 2026 shows as 'Day 1' on 17 Nov 2026, so it reads as if the travellers are already on the trip. The live trip row says: '20 Nov 2026 – 25 Nov 2026 · Day 1 · 1 traveller', with a BOOKED badge. Root cause is in the API, not the UI. In api/app/duty/service.py:258 the code sets day = max(first, t['start_date']), which is the start date for a future trip. Then where_on() at line 172 computes day_no = (day - start_date).days + 1, which is always 1 for that trip. The UI at web/app/(crm)/travelling/page.tsx:74-76 shows 'Leaves <date>' only when day_no is null. Because of this, the 'duty.trip.leaves' branch can never fire for a trip that has not started, and every upcoming departure in the 7- or 14-day window is labelled 'Day 1'. The audit's write guard did not cause this: the page is server-rendered from a GET, and the only blocked request was the Sentry envelope POST. The text is wrong for today's date.
findings.evidence: crm1/crops/travel-1440-light-0.png; re-check recheck-travelling/travel-1440-light.png (trip row text 'BOOKED 20 Nov 2026 – 25 Nov 2026 · Day 1 · 1 traveller'); crm1/api/duty__travelling.json today=2026-11-17, start_date=2026-11-20, on_date=2026-11-20, day_no=1; api/app/duty/service.py:172 and :258; web/app/(crm)/travelling/page.tsx:74
findings.proposal: In duty.travelling, return day_no=null when start_date > today (the local first day of the window). place and the running lines can still come from the start day. That lets the existing 'Leaves <date>' label show. Add a unit test for a trip that starts inside the window but after today.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED by a fresh run on 17/11 05:31 UTC with auth/crm.json (still valid, landed on the page). The page throws a hydration mismatch, 'Minified React error #418 (text)', and the cause is now proven. The server-rendered HTML holds <time> text '17 Nov 2026 05:31' (the ECS runtime is in UTC). After hydration, a browser in Asia/Bangkok shows '17 Nov 2026 12:31' for the same dateTime. The same session with the browser time zone forced to UTC renders with 0 errors and sends 1 Sentry envelope instead of 3, so each load does send 2 extra envelopes. The 12 blocked writes are all of these app-sent Sentry envelope POSTs (3 per load x 4 variants), not user actions, so the audit guard did not cause the error. A related bug is in the same function: whenText() takes the date from formatDate(), which uses Intl with timeZone 'UTC', and the time from toLocaleTimeString in the runtime zone. Between 00:00 and 07:00 local time (UTC+7) a row therefore shows yesterday's date next to today's local time.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED, and the cause is now clear. The two rewrite counters come from different sources. /v1/billing.tours_rewritten is computed in the view shared.v_tenant_monthly_usage (mig 439) as count(DISTINCT gold_aa_internal.tenant_tour_versions) created this month, for EVERY edit_source, tenant_edit versions included. /v1/quota.rewrites_used reads the counter shared.tenant_rewrite_usage. Only _check_and_consume_rewrite_quota() increments that counter, and only trigger_rewrite() calls it. Today's capture has 2 ai_generated versions created on 2026-11-08 (v5 and v6 of the Laos to Vietnam tour), yet /v1/quota returns rewrites_used 0 for 2026-11. Those two versions therefore never consumed quota, which means some path creates AI versions without going through trigger_rewrite, or the counter row is missing. Separately, a tenant edit (the _VERSION_EDIT_INSERT_SQL path, edit_source 'tenant_edit') raises billing.tours_rewritten, and with it the billed overage tours_overage/overage_usd, but never raises the quota counter. The Dashboard says 'Rewrites used 2 / 200'. The Marketplace meter and the Billing usage meter (usageMeter() on /v1/quota in MarketplacePage.tsx:30-31 and PlaceholderTabs.tsx:101/257) say 0 used. Nothing here comes from the audit's write guard, because these are GET responses.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED. I could not reopen the page live: studio.json, crm.json and crm-c2.json had all expired by 12:3x. /bff/me and every /api/tenant read returned 401, and crm.json redirected to /portal-access/none. I judged from the GET bodies saved at 11:51 (studio1/out/api), the screenshots and origin/main code (Partner 9ec86b8a, CIS origin/main). Neither the audit's write guard nor a stale date caused this. What the 11:51 data shows: three requests have a live post that belongs to an OLDER piece. 'Beyond the Shoreline': newest piece 09d6bd4d, created 13 Nov, 25 words; the live post is piece b5f11e37 from 10 Nov. 'What Silence Leaves Behind': newest d6b885d5, created 10 Nov; live post 6aa57cde from 9 Nov. 'The Market as Cultural Decoder': newest 05a5b95b, created 10 Nov; live post dbf45319 from 8 Nov. My Content shows these rows as PUBLISHED with Created later than Published. That part is on purpose: the S251 review rule in myContent.test.ts lines 204-217 says the request is published, the newest text is not publishable, and it cannot be written again. The only signal that the live post holds older text is a tooltip on the small link icon ('openPublishedEarlier'). The real defect is between the two pages. On the Publish page, 'Ready to publish' lists the same three newest piece_ids with an active Publish button (WordPress connected). CIS GET /v1/publish-log/pending only excludes a piece that has its own published/requested publish_log row. It does not check other pieces of the same request. publish() refuses only superseded pieces, and its idempotency key is per piece revision. So one click on the Publish page would put a SECOND WordPress post online for content that My Content calls 'Already published', which is the very thing the S251 rule exists to prevent. A second issue: the 'Created' column shows the newest revision's date next to the old post's date, with no visible note that the live post is older.
findings.evidence: studio1/out/api/_api_tenant_v1_content_writing_reviews.json (11:51): rows 09d6bd4d/b5f11e37 (created 2026-11-13T00:13, published 2026-11-10T14:54), d6b885d5/6aa57cde (2026-11-10T06:18 / 2026-11-09T15:54), 05a5b95b/dbf45319 (2026-11-10T06:17 / 2026-11-08T10:45); _api_tenant_v1_publish_log_pending.json lists 09d6bd4d, d6b885d5, 05a5b95b; _api_tenant_v1_publish_log.json shows only b5f11e37, 6aa57cde, dbf45319 as published. Screenshots portal-content-1440-light.png (PUBLISHED, 13 Nov / 10 Nov) and portal-content-publish-1440-light.png ('Beyond the Shoreline' under Ready to publish with a Publish button). Code: CIS api/routers/v1_publish.py _PENDING_SQL (NOT EXISTS on pl.piece_id = cp.piece_id only) and _publishable_channel (only 'superseded' blocks); Partner web/lib/studio/myContent.ts:341 liveIsEarlierVersion; ReviewList.tsx:350-373; tests/studio/myContent.test.ts:204-217.
findings.proposal: Make the request-wide rule the same on both sides, in CIS. In _PENDING_SQL, also exclude a request that already has a published or requested publish_log row for any of its pieces. In publish(), refuse that case with a 409 such as 'This content is already live (an earlier version). Unpublish it first or update the live post.' In My Content, when liveIsEarlierVersion is true, show it visibly: a 'Live: earlier version' sub-label under the PUBLISHED badge, plus a tooltip on the Created date explaining it is the newer text's date. The audit's original idea (a 'newer version ready' badge with a Publish action) is dropped because it breaks the S251 no-second-post rule.

findings.detail: RE-CHECK S283: CONFIRMED, not refuted. On the agency's own planner, 'Plan from a tour route' proposes Adventure Asia catalogue tours that the agency does not sell, and it shows their AA tour names under the agency's brand. Live re-run on 17/11: GET /api/browse?resource=routes&country=India&days=7 → 200 with 5 proposals ('Cycling Adventure in Meghalaya — 7 Days', 'Kerala Beaches and Backwaters — 7 Days', 'Golden Triangle: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, 8 Days', 'Classic South India: Kochi to Kovalam — 9 days', 'India's Golden Triangle — 8 Days'). None of their source_ids is among the 4 tours of GET /api/browse?resource=tenant-tours&tenant=pilot-rehearsal-01 (total 4: China x1, Sri Lanka x2, Philippines x1, no India). The page itself requests /api/browse?resource=countries and the tiles with no tenant parameter. The 'Heading to…' select lists all 21 catalogue countries. Only the list view call (tenant-tours&tenant=pilot-rehearsal-01) carries the tenant. Code on origin/main (#274, newer than the local checkout at #271): frontend/lib/api.ts fetchRoutes() sends only country and days. frontend/app/api/browse/route.ts maps 'routes' and 'countries' to /browse/routes and /browse/countries without the tenant header. backend/browse/routes.py reads catalog.v_tour_leg / v_tour_stop for the whole catalogue ('need no AA tenant'). RoutePlanner.tsx renders s.tour_name for each segment. The audit's write guard plays no part: these are GET reads. Context for triage: root ADR 0019, amendment S278 (AA-1094), records this as a known deferral: 'The map, search and route finder of an agency's planner still read AA's graph views; a per-tenant graph is a later minor.' The same amendment also states 'TripPlanner never shows AA's text under an agency's brand.' The route finder showing AA tour names, and offering to pin tours the agency has not adopted, conflicts with that rule. Severity stays medium because the gap is known and on record.

findings.proposal: Short term: on /{slug}/plan, either hide the route finder or filter its proposals (and the 'Heading to' countries) to the agency's source_ids from catalog.v_tenant_tour_v1. Pass the tenant slug through fetchRoutes → /api/browse → the Lambda. Longer term: the per-tenant graph minor that ADR 0019 S278 already plans. Get the tech lead's call first on whether agency planners may propose AA tours the agency has not adopted. At minimum, do not show AA tour names under the agency brand.
